commands.label: Focus split left
commands.description: Moves the cursor to the split on the left, like <C-w>h.
examples: Two splits side by side, cursor on the right: SPC w h → cursor is in the left split
commands.rationale: Mirrors Vim <C-w>h: SPC w is the window map in Doom Emacs and proxies <C-w> in LazyVim, and VSpaceCode uses SPC w h.

semantics.vscodevim: SPC w h moves only between editor groups and wraps around at the edge; VSCodeVim's own <C-w>h can also move focus out of the editor area.
semantics.ideavim: Runs IdeaVim's own <C-w>h, which by default moves only between editor splits and stops at the edge, as in Vim.

commands.label: Focus split below
commands.description: Moves the cursor to the split below, like <C-w>j.
examples: Two splits, one above the other, cursor in the top one: SPC w j → cursor is in the bottom split
commands.rationale: Mirrors Vim <C-w>j: SPC w is the window map in Doom Emacs and proxies <C-w> in LazyVim, and VSpaceCode uses SPC w j.

semantics.vscodevim: SPC w j moves only between editor groups and wraps around at the edge; VSCodeVim's own <C-w>j can also move focus out of the editor area.
semantics.ideavim: Runs IdeaVim's own <C-w>j, which by default moves only between editor splits and stops at the edge, as in Vim.

commands.label: Focus split above
commands.description: Moves the cursor to the split above, like <C-w>k.
examples: Two splits, one above the other, cursor in the bottom one: SPC w k → cursor is in the top split
commands.rationale: Mirrors Vim <C-w>k: SPC w is the window map in Doom Emacs and proxies <C-w> in LazyVim, and VSpaceCode uses SPC w k.

semantics.vscodevim: SPC w k moves only between editor groups and wraps around at the edge; VSCodeVim's own <C-w>k can also move focus out of the editor area.
semantics.ideavim: Runs IdeaVim's own <C-w>k, which by default moves only between editor splits and stops at the edge, as in Vim.

commands.label: Focus split right
commands.description: Moves the cursor to the split on the right, like <C-w>l.
examples: Two splits side by side, cursor on the left: SPC w l → cursor is in the right split
commands.rationale: Mirrors Vim <C-w>l: SPC w is the window map in Doom Emacs and proxies <C-w> in LazyVim, and VSpaceCode uses SPC w l.

semantics.vscodevim: SPC w l moves only between editor groups and wraps around at the edge; VSCodeVim's own <C-w>l can also move focus out of the editor area.
semantics.ideavim: Runs IdeaVim's own <C-w>l, which by default moves only between editor splits and stops at the edge, as in Vim.

commands.label: Focus next split
commands.description: Moves the cursor to the next split, wrapping around, like <C-w>w.
examples: Three splits: SPC w w three times → back where you started
commands.rationale: Mirrors Vim <C-w>w; VSpaceCode uses SPC w w.

semantics.vscodevim: SPC w w moves to the next editor group, wrapping around, and takes no count, while Vim's {count}<C-w>w goes to window {count}.
semantics.ideavim: Runs IdeaVim's own <C-w>w, which moves to the next split, wrapping around, or with a count to the split with that number.

commands.label: Split right
commands.description: Opens the current file in a new split on the right and moves there, like <C-w>v.
examples: SPC w v → the file is open side by side, cursor in the new split
commands.rationale: Mirrors Vim <C-w>v; VSpaceCode uses SPC w v and LazyVim SPC |.

semantics.vscodevim: VSCodeVim's own <C-w>v splits in the direction set by workbench.editor.openSideBySideDirection; SPC w v always splits to the right.
semantics.ideavim: Runs IdeaVim's own <C-w>v, which splits the editor side by side and moves the cursor to the new split.

commands.label: Split down
commands.description: Opens the current file in a new split below and moves there, like <C-w>s.
examples: SPC w s → the file is open twice, one above the other
commands.rationale: Mirrors Vim <C-w>s; VSpaceCode uses SPC w s and LazyVim SPC -.

semantics.vscodevim: VSCodeVim's own <C-w>s splits across the direction set by workbench.editor.openSideBySideDirection; SPC w s always splits down.
semantics.ideavim: Runs IdeaVim's own <C-w>s, which splits the editor one above the other and moves the cursor to the new split.

commands.label: Close split
commands.description: Closes the current split with its tabs, like <C-w>c. With a single split, the tabs close and the split remains.
examples: Two splits, cursor in the right one: SPC w c → only the left split is left
commands.rationale: Mirrors Vim <C-w>c: SPC w follows <C-w> and tab commands live under SPC b; LazyVim's SPC w d also runs <C-w>c.

semantics.vscodevim: VSCodeVim's own <C-w>c closes only the active tab; SPC w c closes the editor group with all of its tabs, pinned ones included. With a single group, the tabs close and the empty group remains.
semantics.ideavim: Runs IdeaVim's own <C-w>c, which closes the unpinned tabs of the current split and then the split if no tab is left, so a split with a pinned tab stays open. In the last split it closes the unpinned tabs, where Vim refuses with E444.

commands.label: Close other splits
commands.description: Closes the other splits, like <C-w>o. A split that holds a pinned tab stays open with only its pinned tabs.
examples: Three splits: SPC w o → only the current split is left

semantics.vscodevim: SPC w o closes the unpinned tabs of every other editor group, so a group that holds a pinned tab remains. VSCodeVim's own <C-w>o merges all groups into one instead.
semantics.ideavim: Runs IdeaVim's own <C-w>o, which closes the unpinned tabs of every other split and then each split left without tabs, so a split with a pinned tab stays open.
